decisions.statement: A parse is keyed by the text parsed and by the model that parsed the text.
A text that moves between files keeps the parse already taken.
A cached parse is answered only where the text stored beside the parse is the text asked for.
A line the cache cannot read is skipped rather than repaired.
A skipped line is answered as no parse.
The model reads a skipped line's text again.
Every fault the cache can carry comes back as no parse rather than as a wrong parse.
The cache is filled as a side effect of parsing rather than by a run of its own.
The cache sits under the git directory every worktree of a checkout shares.
A model has a directory named for that model.
Retiring a model is one deletion.
A shard is named by the first two characters of the key.
Setting `AKASHA_PARSE_CACHE_OFF` leaves every parse to the model.
A cache the disk refuses still answers for the life of the process.
No parse the cache has is committed.
Nothing here says the meaning of a parse.

definition: the parse a text was given before, kept so the model reads that text once
